summary: U.S. equity markets opened lower on Monday, August 17, 2026, with the S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq all falling between 0.3% and 0.5% as rising oil prices and climbing Treasury yields weighed on sentiment ahead of a critical week of retail earnings. Oil prices surged as prospects for Middle East peace dimmed, with President Trump rejecting an extension of the Iran ceasefire and threatening further military action if Oman interferes with reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The spike in energy costs revived inflation concerns despite recent soft CPI data. Investors are now laser-focused on results from Walmart, Target, Home Depot, and Lowe's this week, looking for signs of consumer resilience amid high gasoline prices and persistent rate uncertainty. Bitcoin and Ethereum traded mixed near $63,000 and $1,900 respectively, with institutional Bitcoin ETF inflows showing renewed strength after Harvard disclosed a $101 million BTC ETF stake and Jane Street revealed over $1 billion in spot Bitcoin ETF holdings. Fed rate hike odds for September have fallen to 30% following last week's weak retail sales and softer inflation prints.

signals.title: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire extension, oil surges above $88
signals.desc: Trump threatened military action against Oman and rejected ceasefire extension as Iran conflict escalates, driving oil prices sharply higher and reviving inflation fears.

signals.title: Rising Treasury yields and oil pressure equities into retail earnings week
signals.desc: S&P 500 fell 0.5% and Nasdaq dropped 0.3% as 10-year yields climbed and investors de-risked ahead of key consumer spending data from Walmart, Target, and Home Depot.

signals.title: Harvard and Jane Street disclose major Bitcoin ETF stakes
signals.desc: Harvard revealed $101 million in BTC ETF holdings while Jane Street disclosed over $1 billion across IBIT, FBTC, and GBTC, signaling deepening institutional adoption.

signals.title: Fed September rate hike odds collapse to 30% after weak data
signals.desc: Market pricing for a September rate increase fell from 50% to 30% following surprise drop in retail sales and softer-than-expected July inflation prints.

signals.title: Consumer discretionary under pressure as gasoline prices climb
signals.desc: Consumer discretionary stocks remain one of only two S&P 500 sectors down year-to-date as gas prices trade $1 per gallon above pre-Iran war levels ahead of key retail earnings.

verdict: Risk-off tone dominates as Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices overshadow dovish Fed expectations, with retail earnings this week poised to determine whether the consumer can sustain the rally.
